chapter_mission: Veranthos from orbit, descent, and the first night at the valley's edge. The ring structure delivers escalating wrongness. The city has not been destroyed — it has drifted. The Scar is visible in the valley from the ridgeline. Torin stands at the camp edge with the expression of a man coming home.
chapter_turn: Everything converges tomorrow. The book's geography and the book's characters line up on the same clock. Ben does not yet know the content of what is coming; he knows the shape of it, and Torin's silhouette against the stars announces it without a word.

scene_plan.purpose: Orbit over Veranthos. Blue-green oceans, temperate forests, beautiful. Scan data contradicts the beauty — weather patterns not following rotation, vegetation defying sunlight, ocean currents reversed. The seal boundary visible in Force perception as a membrane; beyond it the wound, gravitational. Desh: 'Her ship is on the surface. Valley coordinates. She's already there.' H18 and H19 resolve.

Descent through the ring structure. Ring 4: seal boundary — Ben crosses it and the Force drops away entirely, not thinned but gone. Ring 3: evacuation zone — doors standing open, vehicles pointed away from the valley, a thousand years of overgrowth. Ring 2: the city — homes, shops, a school, a child's toy on a step, vines climbing and reversing, flowers blooming on shadow faces. Desh's grief-without-an-object lands without mysticism. The ridgeline opens on the valley. The Scar — a three-meter vertical distortion where the Force was torn — is visible below. Ben stops walking.

Camp at the valley's edge. Night. The Scar visible against the stars — a line of absence outlined by light. Torin stands at the camp perimeter and has not looked away from the valley since they arrived. His Force presence has softened. He looks younger. More alive. More dangerous. Ben watches from the tent and understands: tomorrow. H20 plants.

relationship_turns.to: present place — the world Ben has been navigating toward for three acts exists under his boots. Its beauty is a symptom. Its silence is architecture. His Force-sense is gone inside the seal boundary. He will operate without it for the rest of the book
already gone — Torin at the camp edge is not with them anymore, and no one pretends he is. The group's composure is performance for Ben's benefit; they are all watching what he will do

grief-without-an-object — the non-Force-sensitive experience of full de-structuring lands in s2. The wound affects everyone; the book's thematic claim about the lattice mattering to non-Force-users becomes physical here

exit_vector: Camp silent on the ridge. Torin's silhouette against the line of the Scar. Veraine already somewhere in the valley. Desh in the tent with his instruments, Sera not watching Torin watch, Kael awake but motionless. The clock is at hours and the chapter closes with Ben understanding that the second plot point is not coming — it is here.
